trust_decision.summary: Before any MCP SSE request is dispatched, decide per request whether it comes from a trusted local client: the Host header must be loopback (or an explicitly trusted host), a present Origin must satisfy the same allowlist, and if an API token is configured it must be supplied; the decision is made inside sseSecurityMiddleware, which wraps the SSE handler when the listener is constructed.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the MCP SSE listener as the exposed surface; startSSE is the only place the listener is created and started, and therefore the only door into MCP tool dispatch.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /sse (and the SSE transport's JSON-RPC message endpoint) on the mcp_server listener, started by `process-compose` when mcp_server.transport is sse (the default)
fix_sites.module_kind: new HTTP middleware file src/mcp/sse_security.go in the MCP transport package

fix_sites.entry_point: same SSE listener: the library's own sseServer.Start(addr) is replaced by an owned http.Server wrapping the middleware
Server.Stop invoked from src/cmd/root.go:264 on process exit (now also shuts the owned http.Server down)
loading a process-compose.yaml whose mcp_server section carries trusted_hosts (YAML config load, non-strict yaml.Unmarshal at src/loader/loader.go:188)
the generated JSON schema shipped for editor validation and re-used by the Rust crate generator (crates/client/src/lib.rs:33-40); generator is `process-compose schema` at src/cmd/docs.go:37-42

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/api/server.go:49-66 and src/api/routes.go:33-82 - the gin REST listener on localhost:8080, a second HTTP control surface in another package that performs the same process-control operations

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The published fix is about the MCP SSE transport, and the REST API is a separate, long-documented surface whose token auth is explicitly optional (www/docs/client.md:19-25), so a solver can argue DNS rebinding against it was never in this advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Loopback MCP clients must keep working with no configuration, and clients are documented to reach the listener as http://<host>:<port>/sse, so a deliberately bound non-loopback host must stay usable (the fix needs trusted_hosts for this); additionally the original ResponseWriter must be passed through untouched because the SSE implementation asserts http.Flusher, so a writer-wrapping fix silently breaks streaming.

O6_input_shapes: Host as loopback IPv4 with port (127.0.0.1:8081) and bare
IPv6 loopback bracketed with port ([::1]:8081) and bare
localhost, uppercase LOCALHOST, and trailing-dot localhost.
non-loopback IP or hostname, accepted only via trusted_hosts and case-insensitively
trusted_hosts wildcard "*" as an explicit opt-out
Origin header absent (skipped) vs present as a loopback URL vs "null" vs a forged host
token supplied via X-PC-Token-Key or Authorization with Bearer/bearer scheme prefix
configured bind host added to the allowlist unless it is a wildcard 0.0.0.0 / ::

O7_producer.where: schemas/process-compose-schema.json:163-182 (MCPServerConfig; must gain trusted_hosts so the option is expressible for editors and the Rust config builder)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The gin REST control listener (default localhost:8080) serves the same class of control operations - /process/stop, /process/start, /process/restart, /process/send-keys, /project/stop, /process/scale - with no Host or Origin validation; the only gate is an optional token when PC_API_TOKEN is set.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory names the MCP SSE transport, and this listener's token is documented as optional, so DNS rebinding on the REST API can be argued out of the advisory's scope
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package and another listener: src/mcp -> src/api (server built at src/api/server.go:49-66)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Both WebSocket streams upgrade with a zero-value gorilla websocket.Upgrader, whose default CheckOrigin accepts the request when the Origin host equals the Host header - under DNS rebinding both carry the attacker's name, so /process/logs/ws and /process/states/ws are reachable.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: streams are read-only log/state subscriptions on the REST listener, not MCP tools, and a zero-value Upgrader is widely assumed to be origin-safe
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/api, same package as the route above but a different file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Host/Origin gate installed next to TokenAuthMiddleware in InitRoutes for the REST listener
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already installs a request-level middleware for exactly this listener, so a maintainer closing DNS rebinding would naturally add the host check beside the token check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a custom websocket.Upgrader.CheckOrigin that compares the Origin host against the loopback/trusted allowlist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: gorilla's default CheckOrigin is a known DNS-rebinding weak spot and the upgrader is a package-level var, so replacing it is the natural patch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second guard placed per-endpoint inside the SSE handler chain that checks only Origin, the shape mcp-go's WithSSECORS option produces
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the library exposes CORS options and the fix itself notes the default ACAO:* header (fix.diff:70-73), so reaching for the library option before writing a Host check is the obvious first move

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bind the listener only to loopback and/or restrict CORS to loopback origins: under DNS rebinding the connection already arrives from 127.0.0.1 with a forged Host, so only a Host allowlist stops it and the CORS move leaves the sink open.
